doorControls.name: I Fucked Up Blastdoor Button of Justice

strings: It's a baseball hat in a tastefull green colour.
A basic, dull, white chef's apron.
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
A transit tube for moving things around.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
Flooring that shows its contents underneath. Engineers love it!
A one meter section of regular pipe.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
A basin used to grow plants in.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
It's a normal black ink pen.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
A thin layer of dust coating the floor.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
A basic wooden fence meant to prevent people like you either in or out of somewhere.
The raptors will eat out of it!
For horses and cows like you.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
Heats or cools gas in connected pipes.
A pipe with a valve that can be used to disable flow of gas through it.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A standard metal table frame covered with an amazingly fancy, patterned cloth.
A warning sign which reads 'HIGH VOLTAGE'.
Used to copy important documents and anatomy studies.
A large vessel containing pressurized gas.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
This little bugger can be used to store and transport ores.
A scanner that checks surrounding rock for useful minerals; it can also be used to stop gibtonite detonations.
Used by engineering and mining staff to see basic structural and terrain layouts through walls, regardless of lighting conditions.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
Nanotrasen patented gravity invariant hourglass. Guaranteed to flow perfectly under any conditions.
A Prism-brand path illumination device. It is anchored in place and glowing steadily.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
It's black and greasy. Looks like Beepsky made another mess.
The linear induction plate that powers the tram.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
What mysteries could this hold? Maybe Research & Development could find out.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
Learn skills with only minimal chance for brain damage.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
A small screen which the AI can use to present itself.
Do jump on it, it can take it.
Converts plants into biomass, which can be used to construct useful items.
A handy little spring-loaded trap for catching pesty rodents.
Great for trams, not so great for skating. This one is a power rail.
Not to be confused with the legally distinct children's toy, this lunar sand is coarse and rough and gets everywhere.
A warning sign which reads 'KEEP CLEAR OF DOCKING AREA'.
Uses an infrared beam to detect passing trams. Works when paired with a sensor on the other side of the track.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
All engineering related spawners go here
A sign labelling the AI's heavily-fortified satellite.
A sign that warns would-be travellers of hostile alien life in the vicinity.
A flimsy framework of iron rods.
A warning sign which reads 'ESCAPE PODS'.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Science department is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Medbay is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the hot stuff is.
You shouldn't see this. Report it please.
A pump that moves gas by pressure.
A telescreen that connects to the cargo and main station camera network.
Jeez. I hope that's not for lunch.
It's still good. Four second rule!
Lead-lined shutters with a radiation hazard symbol. Whilst this won't stop you getting irradiated, especially by a supermatter crystal, it will stop radiation travelling as far.
An underfloor disposal pipe with a sorting mechanism.
Now you see me, now you don't...
Looks painful to step in. Don't mine down.
It's used for removing weeds or scratching your back.
A stylish vendor to dispense the most stylish bar clothing!
It's an underfloor wiring terminal, used to draw power from the grid.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
A large structural assembly made out of metal; It requires a layer of iron before it can be considered a wall.
Somehow, it is not melting under these conditions. Must be some very thick ice. Just as slippery too.
An adapter which allows pipes to connect to other pipenets on different decks.
A cheap Nanotrasen medical laptop, it functions as a medical records computer. It's bolted to the table.
A heads-up display that scans the humanoids in view and provides accurate data about their health status.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
This device is used to trigger station functions which require more than one ID card to authenticate, or to give the Janitor access to a department.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
A complex metal backbone with standard limb sockets and pseudomuscle anchors.
A console used for high-priority announcements and emergencies.
Mirror mirror on the wall, who's the most robust of them all?
It's a secure locker for personnel. The first person to swipe their ID gains control.
It's a storage unit for emergency breath masks and O2 tanks.
A warning sign which reads 'EXTERNAL AIRLOCK'.
A wall-mounted first aid station, designed to treat minor injuries - just stick your hand in and try to relax.
For the exotic art of paper shuffling.
It's a storage unit for level 3 biohazard gear.
It's an M. 7 Reinforced Plunger© for heavy duty plunging.
Yes, that's a functional cannon. Yes, it requires command access to open. No, you can't have it.
The Head of Security's own personal cannon, appropriated after a lengthy battle with raiding pirates. Hasn't seen much use then, thankfully.
A custom security console with added access to the labor camp network.
A raised platform which can make you slightly taller.
A lightweight titanium composite structure with titanium silicate panels.
The subfloor lattice of the tram. You can build a tram wall frame by using titanium sheets, or place down thermoplastic tram floor tiles.
For connecting portables devices related to atmospherics control.
A link to the netverse. It has an assortment of cables to connect yourself to a virtual domain.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
A seedy table for seedy dealings in seedy places.
An interface between crew and the cryogenic storage oversight systems.
A punching bag. Can you get to speed level 4???
Automagically transforms into a random cola vendor. If you see this while in a shift, please create a bug report.
It's a deliciously rectangular sheet of pizza!
HOLY SHEET! That is a lot of glass.
A warning sign which reads 'SECURE AREA'.
A deck of space-grade playing cards.
A luxurious double bed, for those too important for small dreams.
For art pieces hung by the public.

A black ball with a stenciled number eight in white on the side. It seems full of dark liquid. The instructions state that you should ask your question aloud, and then shake.
This refrigerator looks quite dusty, is there anything edible still inside?
A machine that is used to condense strange rocks, useless relics, and broken objects into bigger artifacts.
A slip of paper containing a pearl of wisdom about fishing within it, though you wish it were an actual pearl.
An underfloor disposal pipe which sorts wrapped and unwrapped objects.
This plaque commemorates the fall of the Atmos FEA division. For all the charred, dizzy, and brittle men who have died in its hands.
The Human Harvest: From Seed to Market
Bits of torn, broken, worthless plastic.
A huge chunk of metal with a dial embedded in it. Fine print on the dial reads \"Scarborough Arms - 2 tumbler safe, guaranteed thermite resistant, explosion resistant, and assistant resistant.\"
A wooden board with letters etched into it, used in seances.
A modest sauna oven with rocks. Add some fuel, pour some water and enjoy the moment.

A specialized medical kit for when the ordnance lab -spontaneously- burns down.
A silent polaroid camera with extra capacity for crime investigations.
A board for linking evidence to crimes.
Safely and efficiently extracts excess fat from a subject.
the most uncomfortable chair in the world

\"I'll sweeten thy sad grave: thou shalt not lack the flower that's like thy face, pale primrose, nor the azured hare-bell, like thy veins; no, nor the leaf of eglantine, whom not to slander, out-sweeten'd not thy breath.\"
An interface for ordering fresh produce and other. A far more expensive option than the botanists, but oh well.
A machine with some drapes and a camera, used to update security record photos. Requires Security access to use, and adds a height chart to the person.
A tool used by great men to placate the frothing masses. Can be used to hasten allies with right-click.
A figurine depicting Ian the corgi! HoP's goodest boy.
Used to control a linked teleportation Hub and Station.

Removable disk used to download security-related tablet apps.

A poster glorifying the engineering team.
Fake handcuffs meant for erotic roleplay.

Contains a large reservoir of soft drinks.

A vending machine for dispensing chemistry related clothing.

It is made out of the same material as the station's Black Box and is designed to resist all conventional weaponry. 		There appears to be a small amount of surface corrosion. Due to the expensive material, it was made incredibly small to cut corners, leaving only enough room to fit something as slim as an ID card.
A vending machine for specialised clothing for members of Command.
A medical wrench with common(medical?) uses. Can be found in your hand.
Displays the status of mechs connected to the recharge station.
A raised platform you can perform upon.
A warning sign which reads 'YES SMOKING'.
A head-mounted face cover designed to protect the wearer completely from space-arc eye.
The janitorial department's trusty pet lizard.
A machine that is used to slowly uncover items within strange rocks.
Manufactures circuit boards for the construction of machines.
A generic floppy disk. No way Nanotrasen still uses those, right?

Another of MeLo-Tech's dubiously useful medsci scanners, the disease analyzer is a pretty rare find these days - NT found out that giving their hospitals the lowest-common-denominator pandemic equipment resulted in too much financial loss of life to be profitable. There are rumours that the inbuilt AI is jealous of the first aid analyzer's success.
A crate containing an assortment of cheap prosthetic limbs.
A vending machine rumoured to be capable of dispensing clothing for medical personnel.
NexaCache(tm)! Dubiously authentic gear for the digital daredevil.
This is just a sheet of paper thoroughly covered in what could either be crayon or spraypaint.
You woke them up, and now they're pissed.
A machine that is used to scan strange rocks, making it easier to extract the item inside.
A comfy-looking dog bed. You can even strap your pet in, in case the gravity turns off.
Thanks to the fast and dynamic response of our electrolyzers, on-site hydrogen production is guaranteed. Warranty void if used by clowns
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with engineering programs.
The POWER that gamers CRAVE! In partnership with Vlad's Salad.

An arc furnace, a specialist machine that can rapidly smelt ores using, as the name implies, massive amounts of electricity. While not nearly as fast and efficient as other ore refining methods, the arc furnace is capable of returning larger amounts of refined material than a standard refining process can. A sticker on the side notes that this may exhaust waste gasses to the air during operation.
Tastes just like the chef's soup.
A primitive form of transportation. Place on any floor to start building a railroad.
For the hard-working tradesperson who's in the middle of nowhere and just wants to warm up their pastry-based savoury item from an overpriced vending machine.
Something's bloody meat compressed into a nice solid sheet.
kitty ears or rabbit ears spawner
A nasty looking shard of glass.
A collapsed medical bed that can be carried around.
A sign labelling an area where cargo ships dock.
A hardlight gate with an ID scanner attached to the side. Good at deterring even the most persistent temporarily embarrassed employee.
A broken piece of disposal pipe.
\"In case of emergency, please use the stairs.\" Thus, always use the stairs.
BREAK GLASS IN CASE OF EMERGENCY
A machine for all your detective needs, as long as you need clothes.
A portable tablet that allows you to draw. Legends say these can earn the owner a fortune in some sectors of space.
Important notices from the Chief Engineer.
Old will forever be in fashion.
It's a tool for cutting grafts off plants or changing podperson looks.
There's no label on this wine bottle.
Renault's bed! Looks comfy. A foxy person needs a foxy pet.
A marvel of bureaucratic engineering encased in an efficient plastic shell. It can be refilled with a hand labeler refill roll and linked to buttons with a multitool.
Instead of a license plate number, this could contain a quote like \"Live laugh love\".
Spare tool vending. What? Did you expect some witty description?
You know, we're making a lot of license plates for a station with literally no cars in it.
Used to send criminals to the Labor Camp.
A disk for storing technology data for further research.
A wall made of solid stone bricks.
This mycelium grows into something horrible.
A pole fastened to the ceiling and floor, used to show of one's goods to company.
Fishing anywhere, anytime... anyway what was I talking about?

Poly the Parrot. An expert on quantum cracker theory.
It has a Nanotrasen symbol on it, and was woven with a revolutionary new kind of thread guaranteed to have 0.01% permeability for most non-chemical substances, popular among most modern captains.
I hope I get one that actually matches my meal.
Turn your Good Assistant Points punchcards in here for a payout based on the amount of punches you have, and get a new card!
A figurine depicting a Detective wearing their iconic trench coat.
A combat shotgun gutted and refitted with an internal disabler system. The power supply unit seems to have suffered during The Great Burgerstation Riots of '69
A warning sign which reads 'HARD VACUUM AHEAD'.
A remote control switch for a mounted igniter.
A figurine depicting someone with a long, silky beard wearing a wizard outfit. Warlocks wish they had anything on this.
A telescopic roasting stick with a miniature shield generator designed to ensure entry into various high-tech shielded cooking ovens and firepits.
A figurine depicting the glorious head of the Engineering department.
With one of these stickers, inform the crew that the contraption in the corridor is COMPLETELY SAFE!
A figurine depicting a Shaft Miner holding a survival knife.
A large wooden barrel for holding gunpowder. You'll need to take from this to load the cannons.
A stack of heavy plasteel cannonballs. Gunnery for the space age!
This book was found inside a coffin of a long dead Curator. It is said to be able to reveal the true nature of those who feed upon mankind.
It's slippery and gooey. Perhaps it's the chef's cooking?
A failed experiment of Nanotrasen to create weaponised carp technology. This less than intimidating carp now serves as the Head of Security's pet.
A Modello 3 Coffeemaker that brews coffee and holds it at the perfect temperature of 176 fahrenheit. Made by Piccionaia Home Appliances.
Turn anything and everything into something vaguely alive!
Chance to spawn a rare shiny version.
An adorable stuffed toy that resembles a space carp.

A highly precise directional sensor array which measures the release of quants from decaying tachyons. The doppler shifting of the mirror-image formed by these quants can reveal the size, location and temporal affects of energetic disturbances within a large radius ahead of the array.

A surprisingly heavy yellow winter coat with reflective orange stripes. It has a small wrench for its zipper tab, and the inside layer is covered with a radiation-resistant silver-nylon blend. Because you're worth it.
A crafting bench fitted with tools, securing mechanisms, and a steady surface for blacksmithing.
A figurine depicting a Chaplain hopefully praying for good things.
Contains a small supply of pipes, water recyclers, and iron to connect to the rest of the station.
A glass lab container for storing interesting creatures.
A durable and easily mounted barricade made from metal plates, often used for rapid fortification. Repairing it requires a welder.
A heretical poster depicting the titular star of an equally heretical book.
A trash bin, place your trash here for the janitor to collect.
This poster has one word on it, 'ULTRA'; it depicts a smiling pill next to a beaker. Ominous.
A figurine depicting a Cyborg, the lowest of low.
A type of plumbing constructor designed to rapidly deploy the machines needed for logistics regarding fluids.
Box full of scum-bag tracking utensils.
Box of stuff used to implant chemicals.
When it says walk it means WALK!
A holy diver seeking its target.

An advanced machine equipped with state of the art bomb prediction software that's capable of implosion-compressing raw anomaly cores into finished artifacts. 	Comes with a built-in stabilization and sound-supressant field that consumes a lot of power to prevent obnoxious shaking and sounds heard station-wide, as not to wake up any dorms users.
A telescreen that connects to the minisat's camera network.
WEEEEOOO. WEEEEEOOO. STOP THAT MONKEY. WEEEOOOO.
A little cleaning robot, he looks so excited!
A teleportation matrix used to retrieve boulders excavated by mining NODEs from ore vents.
Protects your hearing from loud noises, and quiet ones as well.
It would seem it vends dyes, and other stuff to make you pretty.
The Film Noir: Proper Procedures for Investigations
Used to remotely scan objects and biomass for DNA and fingerprints. Can print a report of the findings.
A hulking computational machine designed to fabricate virtual domains.
A machine used to deposit and withdraw station funds.
A figurine depicting a Bartender looking stylish with their rockin shades and tophat.
Only intended for binding paper products.
Used to crystallize or solidify gases.

This biochip integrates with user's brain to enable the mastery of a specific skill. Consult certified Nanotrasen neurosurgeon before use. 	There's a little face etched into the back of the skillchip, with buck teeth and goofy-looking glasses.
A fluctuating forcefield for ships to cross.
A split open garbage bag, its stinking content seems to be partially liquified. Yuck!
Some say a barbers best tool is his electric razor, that is not the case. These are used to cut hair in a professional way!
An ailing, old, repurposed cargo hauler. Most of its equipment wires are frayed or missing and its frame is rusted.
It's a little piece of Eden.
It's spicy! Wait... IT'S BURNING ME!!
It's pretty bland, but oh the possibilities...
It's so sour, your face will twist.
Jerry the cat is not amused.
A small electronic device able to chill their surroundings.
A cell charging rack for multiple batteries.
A poster instructing the viewer not to ask about things they aren't meant to know.
Cargo's pet sloth. About as useful as the rest of the techs.
A long list of rules to be followed when in the library, extolling the virtues of being quiet at all times and threatening those who would dare eat hot food inside.
A strangely translucent and iridescent crystal.
An industrial grade pump, capable of either siphoning or spewing liquids. Needs to be anchored first to work. Has a limited capacity internal storage.
WARNING: These devices are extremely dangerous and can cause blindness or deafness in repeated use.
A terrible, terrible thing. It's really awful!
WARNING: These devices are extremely dangerous and can cause blindness and skin irritation.
A computer used to control a nearby holodeck.
A vending machine serving up only the finest of human college student food.
Contains pills used as a last resort means to temporarily stabilize depression and anxiety. WARNING: side effects may include slurred speech, drooling, and severe addiction.
A very complex router and transmitter capable of connecting electronic devices together. Looks fragile.
A machine with some drapes and a camera, used to update security record photos. Requires Law Office access to use.
For all ages*! Doesn't contain any* amount of nicotine. Health and safety risks can be read on the tip of the cigarette.
Goes great with a glass of warm milk.
A keg, usually filled with some low-grade, Nanotrasen brewed alcoholic drink.
A machine used by the quantum server. Quantum code converges here, materializing decrypted assets from the virtual abyss.
A camera that can be used to display whomever is in front of it across all status displays. 		Pair with a greenscreen for best results.
Cuban Pete is in the house!
Used to create a convincing illusion of a different background.
These tactical gloves appear to be unique, made out of double woven durathread fibers which make it fireproof as well as acid resistant
A folding kit that is ideally filled with surgical tools and specialized treatment options for many harder-to-treat wounds.
The control unit of a Modular Outerwear Device, a powered suit that protects against various environments.
A poster advertising syndicate pistols as being 'classy as fuck'. It is covered in faded gang tags.
Several lumps of snow put together to form a snowman.
A top hat worn by only the most prestigious hat collectors.
Used to reclaim your items after you finish your sentence at the labor camp.
Not known for their pleasant disposition.
A perfectly legitimate poster that seems to advertise the very real and genuine method of charging your PDA in the future: microwaves.

A plastic-paneled microwave oven, capable of doing anything a standard microwave could do. 		This one is special designed to be tightly packed into a shape that can be easily re-assembled 		later from the factory. There don't seem to be included instructions on getting it folded back 		together, though...
Used to retrieve cell lines from organisms. Don't worry, it won't sting.
A bag containing fresh, dry coffee arabica beans. Ethically sourced and packaged by Waffle Corp.
This box is shaped on the inside so that only light tubes and bulbs fit.
A device to automatically replace lights. Refill with broken or working light bulbs, or sheets of glass.
Manufactured by UhangInc, used to blind and down an opponent quickly.
Dispenses countless types of pipes. Very useful if you need pipes.
Store your trophies of accomplishment in here, and they will stay forever.
A tank of compressed carbon dioxide for use as propulsion in zero-gravity areas. Painted black to indicate that it should not be used as a source for internals.
A toolbox painted hot pink. Full of crafting supplies!
A toolbox painted bright green. Why anyone would store art supplies in a toolbox is beyond you, but it has plenty of extra space.
This poster depicts a 'HONK' class mech ontop of a stage, next to a pole.
Keeps cold things cold and hot things cold.
A measuring tape specifically produced to measure the depth that has been dug into strange rocks.
A spring loaded gun designed to fit syringes, used to incapacitate unruly patients from a distance.

An infinitely useful device for those finding themselves in a frontier without a stable source of nutrients for crops. 		Using a simplified version of the chemistry dispenser's synthesizer process, it can create hydroponics nutrients out of nothing 		but good old electricity.
A figurine depicting an Atmospheric Technician holding an unlit welder.
Wow! With enough of these, you could buy a bike! ...Pssh, yeah right.
Use this button after you've served someone to tell the next person to come forward.
Operates the photobooth from a distance, allowing people to update their security record photos.
A poster condemning the station's security forces.
A console for assigning civilian bounties to inserted ID cards, and for controlling the bounty pad for export.
Known for their milk, just don't tip them over.
An altar which allows the head of the church to choose a sect of religious teachings as well as provide sacrifices to earn favor.
A hand-held environmental scanner which reports current gas levels.

A vending machine which vends food, as required by section 47-C of the NT's Prisoner Ethical Treatment Agreement. 			This one, however, processes labor points for its products if the user is incarcerated.
A computer system running a deep neural network that processes arbitrary information to produce data useable in the development of new technologies. In layman's terms, it makes research points.
A rectangular steel crate. It seems to be painted to look like silver.
An ore vent, brimming with underground ore. It's already supplying the station with iron and glass.
They look like human remains. They have a strange aura about them.
A box claiming to contain evidence bags.
A rectangular steel crate. It seems to be painted to look like gold.
Here's your chance, do your dance at the Space Jam.
As seen in your favourite Japanese cartoon.
Glass which seems to have rods or something stuck in them.

The Quartermaster's very own gold plated Desert Eagle folded over a million times by superior martian gunsmiths. Excessive use against trespassers has rendered this gun unreliable, at best. Uses .50 AE ammo.
You'd think this thing would be more useful in here.
A weapon that can only be used to its full potential by the truly robust.
A drink served in a classy mug.
Careful, cold ice, do not chew.
A very manly slab of meat.

A pile of raw crab meat.

Central Command standard issue inspection device. 		Used for precision scans to determine if an item contains, or is itself, contraband.
A salvaged syndicate device gutted of its explosives to be used as a training aid for aspiring bomb defusers.
A large thermal battery that projects a high amount of energy when powered.

A scaffold for bees to build honeycomb on.
She's the queen of bees, BZZ BZZ!

A copy of the first run of Captain's Aid ever released. Functionally the same as the later batches, just more expensive. For the truly aristocratic.
A telescreen that connects to the bomb test site's camera.

A frontiersman's classic, closer to a shortsword than a knife. It boasts a full-tanged build, a brass handguard and pommel, a wicked sharp point, and a large, heavy blade, It's almost everything you could want in a knife, besides portability. Seems a little dull due to excessive use against space bears.
A trap used to catch bears and other legged creatures.
A figurine depicting a reptillian Cargo Technican, busy with nonexistent paperwork.
The output side of a turbine generator, contains the turbine and the stator.
A cart for use on rails. Or off rails, if you're so inclined.
Wall-mounted Medical Equipment dispenser, Meant to be used in medical emergencies.
A machine that will recover the damaged, destroyed objects found within the strange rocks.
What is this? Who put it on this station? And why does it emanate strange energy?

The second most common generator design in the galaxy, second only to the P.A.C.M.A.N. The S.O.F.I.E. (Stationary Operating Fuel Ignition Engine) is similar to other generators in burning sheets of plasma in order to produce power. Unlike other generators however, this one isn't as portable, or as safe to operate, but at least it makes a hell of a lot more power. Must be bolted to the ground and attached to a wire before use. A massive warning label wants you to know that this generator outputs waste heat and gasses to the air around it.

Experimental Xeon Particle Entropy Reaction Infuser or something like that. Nanotrasen's new reaction infuser, with a slight less tendency to catastrophically fail than the previous model... or so they say.
Used to help draw the rabble into your bar. Some assembly required. This one doesn't have an access lock.
A modified version of the Type 5 laser gun. Fires entirely harmless bolts of directed energy. Safe AND entertaining to fire with abandon.
A telescreen with access to the research division's camera network.
The cornerstone of any customer service job. This one's been modified for hyper-performance.
A label on the side of this potato reads \"Product of Donk Co. Toys and Recreation department.\" You can attack anyone with it to put it on them instead, if they have a free hand to take it!
This informational poster uses Safety Moth™ to tell the viewer to hide in lockers when the Supermatter Crystal has delaminated, to prevent hallucinations. Evacuating might be a better strategy.
A receiving beacon for bluespace teleportations.
A blue nightcap for all the dreamers and snoozers out there.
Used to monitor the crew's PDA messages, as well as request console messages.
A small contraption designed to imbue a few drinks with a pleasant chill.
You can be totally screwy with this.
Is it cotton? Linen? Denim? Burlap? Canvas? You can't tell.
This is a highly valuable statue made from gold.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with command programs.
A periodic table of the elements, from Hydrogen to Oganesson, and everything inbetween.
Paint for restyling unattached robotic limbs. Sadly doesn't shine like chrome.

A pump bottle containing mexican coffee-flavoured liqueur syrup. In production since 1936, HONK.
A pump bottle containing korta syrup. A sweet, sugary substance made from crushed sweet korta nuts.
A pump bottle containing caramelized sugar, also known as caramel. Do not lick.
A neat small wooden box, holding all your favorite coffee condiments.
A hand-held scanner for analyzing someones gene sequence on the fly. Use on a DNA console to update the internal database.
Filled to the brim with medical junk.
A low-end laptop often used for personal recreation.
Chief Medical Officer's Office Containing Office Space
You've never felt more free than when sleeping on this.
It's a sick-looking goose, probably ate too much maintenance trash. Best not to move it around too much.
A telescreen that connects to the engine waste camera network.
A one-way shuttle console, used to summon the shuttle to the labor camp.
A manifold composed of regular pipes.

An oily condiment made from egg yolks.

Accepts boulders and refines non-metallic ores into sheets using internal chemicals.
A machine that processes and routes PDA and request console messages.
A timeworn shaft, almost totally mined out. With a bit of effort you might be able to haul something up.
A flask of holy water...it's been sitting in maintenance a while though.
